time.desc: The accusing party filed a lawsuit against the accused party on civil grounds such as "personality rights/sexual harassment infringement" and the case was filed by the court, and the dispute entered the judicial process.
This civil dispute has completed several closed court hearings and has entered the stage of waiting for judgment due to procedural adjustments and extension of trial cutoffs.

A public information compilation page appeared on the Internet platform in the name of "Solidarity", which concentrated on disclosing the personal information of the parties and triggered cross-platform spread of controversy.

The court made a first-instance judgment on the civil dispute, finding that the existing evidence was insufficient to establish the elements of sexual harassment and rejecting the plaintiff's claim. At the same time, it made a principled evaluation of the behavior of both parties.

The university involved issued a notice regarding the controversy caused by the judgment, stating that it respects judicial decisions and initiated an investigation and review of existing disciplinary actions and related academic integrity issues.
Content platforms issue governance announcements and permanently ban accounts that pretend to be related to parties and spread false information.
The losing party in the first instance appeals against the first instance judgment and the appeal is accepted by the second instance court, and the case enters the second instance procedure.
The dissertation involved was removed from the academic resource platform, and relevant parties said they were verifying the basis and process for the removal.
